title: TF rollback & upgrade sanity checklist for VPC/on-prem
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + troubleshooting notes for rolling upgrades and, when necessary, rollbacks for VPC / on-prem private deployments. Focus is on common terraform module edge-cases, preflight sanity checks, runtime failures we see in the field, and fast mitigations so customer apps remain available.

Quick context / intended audience:
- For SREs, Solutions Engineers, and on-call engs doing: terraform apply for infra module updates, helm/operator upgrades, or rolling runtime binary changes.
- Not an exact runbook for one site — adapt to the customer topology (AZs, node counts, GPU types).

Top-level plan (high-level):
1) PRE-FLIGHT: TF plan + infra checks + backups
2) CANARY: small subset (1 node pool / 1 replica) upgrade
3) VERIFY: run smoke tests, perf baselines, basic evals
4) ROLL: rolling upgrade with health gates
5) POST: validation, metrics, snapshot state, and optional cleanup
6) ROLLBACK (if health gates fail): revert TF + restart only affected services

Pre-flight terraform and environment checks (must do before apply):
- Confirm state lock: terraform plan against remote state (s3/consul/gs) and ensure no locks. If lock exists, talk to owner — do NOT force unlock without owner.
- Provider/module versions pinned? Look at root module and modules/* versions. Note: aws provider >= 5.0 has subtle IAM ordering changes we've seen cause attach/detach race on ENIs.
- Take remote state backup: copy state to artifact bucket (timestamped).
- Check drift: run `terraform plan -refresh=true` and scan for differences. If non-trivial drift, fix before upgrading.
- Confirm workspace, env vars, and secrets are correct (TF_VAR_*, KMS keys access). Common mistake: wrong AWS profile / assume-role expiration.
- Validate module inputs: subnet CIDR sizes, max_pods, MTU settings for CNI. MTU mismatch = frequent connectivity after upgrade.
- Module edge-case notes:
  - aws_vpc: if using multiple nat gateways, ensure route tables are consistent across AZs (we had INF-5872 where NAT removal cut off ECR access).
  - state splits: avoid moving modules between statefiles mid-upgrade unless you have an explicit plan and snapshot.
  - taints: Use `terraform apply -target` sparingly — prefer full plans unless speed is critical.

Canary upgrade checklist (single AZ / single node pool):
- Mark 1 node as canary via label (k8s) and set Concurrency=1 for canary deployment.
- Drain node gracefully: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Watch for pods that can't come up due to node constraints (GPU driver mismatch).
- Apply infra change to canary only (if possible) or perform helm/operator upgrade on canary.
- Smoke tests (see below) must pass on canary before proceeding.

Smoke-test checklist (quick, automatable):
- infra health: all k8s nodes Ready, no CrashLoopBackOff, kube-proxy running. `kubectl get nodes; kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide`
- control-plane reachability: API server latency < 150ms internal, no 5xx.
- networking: canary pod -> ecr/gcr/registry pull OK, DNS resolution good from pods `nslookup` or `dig`.
- GPU health: `nvidia-smi` returns devices and driver version matches expected.
- filesystem: /var/lib/docker or /var/lib/containerd has > 10% free.
- inference sanity: send a 64-token generation request to the sandbox model endpoint. Check 1) returns within SLO, 2) tokens coherent (not repeated failure token), 3) memory/CPU usage not explosive.
- streaming fallback: test server stream endpoint to confirm chunked responses not broken.
- KV / cache verification: if prefix cache enabled, confirm warm cache hit for a known prefix (run generate twice, second should be faster).
- routing policy test: if model fallback configured, intentionally saturate preferred model until fallback triggers then confirm response correctness.

Common installation/runtime failures and quick triage tips:
- ImagePullBackOff on runtime pods:
  - Check node IAM / registry creds (ECR auth token expired).
  - `kubectl describe pod` -> image pull errors, `kubectl get secret` for docker-registry secret.
- Init container failing due to filesystem permissions:
  - Check PodSecurityPolicy / SELinux settings. Some customers run SELinux strict; ensure operators set proper filecontext or use fsGroup.
- GPU errors (model fails to load):
  - Symptoms: process dies on model load, dmesg shows "NVRM" or kernel Oops, /var/log/messages shows driver mismatch.
  - Quick fixes: reboot node (last resort), reinstall NVIDIA driver, confirm container runtime uses correct nvidia runtime. Check `nvidia-container-cli info`.
- mmap / OOM mmap failure when loading quantized model:
  - Often due to overcommit settings or low memlock/u limits. Check `ulimit -l`, container memory/cgroup limits, and kernel overcommit: `sysctl vm.overcommit_memory`.
- Bind mount permission denied (/dev/nvidia0):
  - Check container runtime has `--gpus` mapping and runtimeClass is configured. Pod must also run with required capabilities.
- TLS handshake failures to control plane or external registry:
  - Confirm CA bundles used by nodes; some on-prem NAT/its middleboxes replace certs. Check `curl -vv` from node to endpoint.
- CNI networking issues after scaling subnets:
  - Symptoms: Pods in specific nodes cannot reach others. Fix: check MTU, iptables rules, and whether the CNI plugin reconciled new MTU.

Log queries and patterns (fast grep):
- runtime container: `kubectl logs -n redwood runtime-pod -c runtime | tail -200` then grep for: "panic", "OOM", "segfault", "model load error", "quantize error"
- node kernel OOM: `dmesg | grep -i oom`
- docker/containerd: `journalctl -u containerd -n 400` or `docker logs CONTAINER`
- systemd GPU errors: `journalctl -k -g NVRM`

Rollback-specific notes (TF state + runtime):
- When to rollback: canary fails critical smoke tests or we see sustained 5xx across >20% of requests for 10+ minutes.
- Rollback steps:
  1) Stop further rollout (pause CI/CD / gates).
  2) Revert the infra change in VCS and run `terraform plan` to ensure the revert is safe.
  3) Apply revert to minimal scope first (e.g., node pool config) — avoid destroying resources that hold data (PV, statefulsets).
  4) For helm/operator changes, rollback the Release: `helm rollback <release> <rev>` and monitor.
  5) If model runtime binary upgrade caused failure, revert the image tag and restart pods.
  6) Collect full logs and attach to ticket, include `kubectl describe` of failed pods and `terraform plan` of the revert.
- State drift edge-case: if revert fails because terraform plan wants to destroy-and-recreate, do NOT proceed without SRE review. Consider manual reconcile or consult infra-owner.

Post-upgrade validation (post-rollback if applicable):
- Validate metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency within baseline ±15%.
- Cost telemetry: token/sec and GPU utilization back to prior levels.
- Run a small evaluation set of prompts (10-20) from customer regression suite.
- Snapshot logs and kube-state for 72 hours and attach to incident.

Debug commands cheat sheet (save locally):
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
- `kubectl get pods -A | egrep "CrashLoopBackOff|Error|ImagePullBackOff"`
- `kubectl describe pod <pod>` and `kubectl logs -c <container> <pod>`
- `ssh node; sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`
- `nvidia-smi -q | grep Driver`
- `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` then `terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.'` (careful with secrets)

Notes to self / TODOs: (quick scribbles)
- Add automated terraform preflight script to check provider versions and lock state — aim for CLI wrapper by Q1.
- Create small k6/vegabomb perf harness for in-cluster inference smoke tests.
- Investigate automated rollback marker in the console that can pause rollouts.
- Confirm upgrade playbook for customers using on-prem H100 vs A100 (different driver pins).

Known unresolved issues / open questions:
- Some customers with strict SELinux policies need a different filesystem mount strategy. Need a canonical doc + a one-click example for operator values. (See INF-5999).
- How to better handle terraform state migrations for multi-tenant customers without long maintenance windows?

Appendix: useful links and commands
- Jenkins/CI job: infra-deploy-private (link internal)
- GitHub PR for last TF change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/312
- Incident reference: INF-5872 (NAT removal caused ECR pulls to fail)

End of doc.

-- Aisha (working draft, keep short bullets; expand into formal runbook when time)
